facts.claim: TSB-AD repo exists at github.com/TheDatumOrg/TSB-AD and its LICENSE file is Apache License 2.0
Benchmark contains 1070 high-quality time series from 40 datasets
Benchmark paper 'The Elephant in the Room: Towards A Reliable Time-Series Anomaly Detection Benchmark' (Liu and Paparrizos) is in the NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track
README recommends VUS-PR as the most reliable measure for time-series anomaly detection (AUC-PR not named)
Datasets are hosted outside GitHub at thedatum.org (zip files for TSB-AD-U and TSB-AD-M)
README claims 40 detection algorithms, but its tables name 35 entries (18 statistical, 12 neural, 5 foundation-model)
Official evaluation lists have 350 univariate and 180 multivariate series, tuning lists 48 and 20
Per-dataset licences for the 40 source collections are published and permit redistribution
Dataset preprocessing and curation are Apache-2.0 (per README disclaimer; the per-dataset licence page it cites returned 404)
Leaderboard univariate VUS-PR about 0.42 and multivariate about 0.35

v1.kill_reason: Not killed. Blocking condition: dataset licences are not found (Lic 2). Shipping the tuning split and eval data cannot be cleared until the per-dataset licences are checked. If any source forbids redistribution, this becomes K6.

Band.why: No dated public agent trials on this task; family shift limits gains; cannot confirm frontier vs reference band

Build.why: About 3 days: licence clearance, data packaging, wrapper, family split

Fit.why: CPU-only fit plausible; foundation-model detectors may exceed the CPU budget

Hor.why: Detector runs and tuning are long, but the core engineering is ensembling plus a wrapper

Lic.why: Code Apache-2.0 confirmed; dataset licences not found, so shipping data is unverified

Multi.why: Per-family and per-detector buckets give continuous credit, but the main lever is one (ensembling)

Nov.why: Closest seed neighbour 0.448 (S-rs-019, subject unverified); 2026 TSB-AD papers are research, not tasks; not crowded

Real.why: Real NeurIPS 2024 D&B repo, Apache-2.0 code, active; dataset provenance mixed and unverified

Ref.why: Reference is a tuned ensemble of public detectors, not a complete implementation; OOD score unmeasured

Seal.why: Hidden families are public upstream; sealing relies on withholding them from the image

Surf.why: 1070 series, but the held-out family split is coarse (about 9 domains), so the graded set is small and noisy

spike_plan.kill_if: Any source dataset forbids redistribution (then K6), or no ensemble beats the best single detector on the held-out domain, or scoring is non-deterministic.
spike_plan.pass_if: All sampled dataset licences permit redistribution, the ensemble beats the best single detector on the held-out domain, and the foundation-model detector fits the CPU budget.
steps: Locate per-dataset licences for the 40 TSB-AD source collections (LICENSE of TSB-AD dataset zips or the cited homepage); record any that forbid redistribution.
Clone TheDatumOrg/TSB-AD at 303dffb in a throwaway container with network; install deps; run the test suite once to get a build verdict.
Download the univariate tuning split only; choose ~10 series across 3-4 domains.
Run 5 cheap detectors and 1 foundation-model detector on those series; time each on 8 CPU cores.
Compute VUS-PR per detector per series; build a naive rank- or z-normalised mean ensemble; compare with the best single detector.
Hold out one whole domain as a pseudo-family and check the ensemble still beats the best single detector on it.
Run the scoring twice to confirm determinism.

v1.summary: TSB-AD is a real, Apache-2.0 NeurIPS 2024 benchmark (1070 series, 40 datasets) with VUS-PR as its recommended metric, so a family-held-out ensemble task is well grounded. The main risks are unverified per-dataset licences (blocks bundling data) and an unmeasured reference, so this is a conditional pass pending the licence check and the 55-minute spike.
